deckTitle: Human Nature Uncut — Hilfe ich bin ein Mensch

cards.power: Replaces the 'Every Man for Himself' rule with the 'Cooperation Engine.' Building complex life over 4 billion years.
cards.lore: Evolution is not a solo deathmatch; cooperation is its ultimate master architect.
cards.gradeReason: You immediately know what to build and how to play it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: naturalist sketch. Subject: beaver drafting a DNA double-helix blueprint. Mood: industrious genius.

cards.power: Activates Super-Altruism, Language, and Shared Childcare to out-compete all other solo predators.
cards.lore: The human animal's true superpower isn't teeth or claws—it's weaponized teamwork.
cards.gradeReason: Instantly embodies the apex cooperative animal. Zero explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action-sketch. Subject: meerkats standing shoulder-to-shoulder radiating light. Mood: triumphant solidarity.

cards.power: Distributes the excruciating biological cost of raising offspring across the entire village network.
cards.lore: We are successful because we are not meant to raise our young alone.
cards.gradeReason: Clear concept, needs table context to activate the roleplay.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm sketch. Subject: penguin colony passing chicks between adults. Mood: communal tenderness.

cards.power: Broadcasts internal emotional data to strangers at the speed of light, bypassing verbal deceit.
cards.lore: Face evolved as an involuntary beacon to establish instantaneous trust in the wild.
cards.gradeReason: Play it and your face becomes the game. Instantly performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: expressive ink. Subject: chameleon on a stick, face radiating truth-waves. Mood: transparent honesty.

cards.power: Deals catastrophic cardiovascular and immune damage daily, equivalent to 15 cigarettes, to isolated entities.
cards.lore: We are biologically tethered; unwanted solitude is lethal to the meat-sack.
cards.gradeReason: Haunting archetype. You see it, you feel it, you don't need a rule.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholy ink. Subject: toad alone smoking in the rain, city lights blurred behind. Mood: existential isolation.

cards.power: Grants a permanent +10 Months to the user's life expectancy.
cards.lore: Believing that your fellow creatures are fundamentally decent literally keeps you from dying.
cards.gradeReason: Strong science hook, but the +10 months needs context to land at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: apothecary sketch. Subject: golden retriever holding glowing vial labelled TRUST. Mood: earnest wonder.

cards.power: Deploys a targeted cellular defense matrix that repels physical and psychological pathogens.
cards.lore: Social support isn't a luxury; it is the frontline of the biological immune system.
cards.gradeReason: Play it and you hug. Full stop. Immediate embodied action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm ink. Subject: large bear enveloping a small creature in a full body hug. Mood: protective warmth.

cards.power: Instantly restores 15% of daily psychological health points for zero cost via a stranger interaction.
cards.lore: Even a fleeting, friendly exchange with an unknown entity significantly elevates baseline well-being.
cards.gradeReason: Good science, slightly mechanical stat-framing slows the embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: deep-sea sketch. Subject: anglerfish and small fish making brief eye contact in the dark. Mood: surprising warmth.

cards.power: Allows pre-verbal infants to instinctively detect and favor 'Helpers' over 'Hinderers.'
cards.lore: Morality isn't drilled into us by civilization; it comes pre-installed in the factory settings.
cards.gradeReason: Describes infant science rather than inviting the player to inhabit a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scientific sketch. Subject: fox kit holding a spinning moral compass in tiny paws. Mood: innate certainty.

cards.power: Overrides childish greed, forcing equal distribution of any co-op mission.
cards.lore: When work is shared, human nature naturally demands an equal split of the rewards.
cards.gradeReason: Play it and you immediately become the furious toddler demanding fairness. Knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: exasperated ink. Subject: kitten slicing a log perfectly in half with tiny axe. Mood: righteous indignation.

cards.power: Triggers absolute psychological rejection of rigged systems and unfair payouts.
cards.lore: We would rather have nothing at all than accept a system that treats us unfairly.
cards.gradeReason: Names an abstract psychological tendency without giving the player a role to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political sketch. Subject: fox in suit staring at rigged scale, shaking head. Mood: seething refusal.

cards.power: The higher the cash value inside the wallet, the higher the probability it gets returned.
cards.lore: Cynics are wrong; trusting people with high stakes actually triggers their inner honor.
cards.gradeReason: Counterintuitive finding gives it punch, but the mechanic needs unpacking at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir ink. Subject: raccoon passing back a fat wallet, conscience visible as glowing orb. Mood: unexpected decency.

cards.power: Acts with pure, unadulterated selfishness, maximizing personal profit at all costs.
cards.lore: A phantom menace; only 7% of the population actually fits this dismal economic model.
cards.gradeReason: The ultimate villain archetype in a deck about human goodness. Plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical caricature. Subject: cat atop a money pile with a 7% pie chart as halo. Mood: smug delusion.

cards.power: Maintains systemic harmony as long as the 60-70% cooperative majority outnumbers the free-riders.
cards.lore: Society collapses only when the cooperative majority realizes they are being played by the selfish minority.
cards.gradeReason: Strong image but the 60-70% threshold makes it analytical rather than immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dynamic sketch. Subject: ants in tug-of-war, majority side glowing. Mood: tense equilibrium.

cards.power: Unleashes lethal aggression—but only when the sacred bonds of the community are threatened.
cards.lore: Humans lack an innate drive to kill; aggression is a secondary defense mechanism for love.
cards.gradeReason: Beautiful paradox: the spiky protector. You know exactly who you are at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fierce ink. Subject: porcupine with quills fully raised, tiny duckling sheltered behind. Mood: protective fury.

cards.power: Activates an innate 'Kill-Inhibition,' causing the entity to intentionally miss their targets in combat.
cards.lore: The hardest thing to teach a human to do is to take the life of another human.
cards.gradeReason: Devastatingly specific. You play the soldier who can't pull the trigger. Instant embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: war sketch. Subject: armored hedgehog aiming rifle but barrel tilts skyward. Mood: conscience overriding orders.

cards.power: Hijacks the brain's reward center, pumping raw dopamine into the bloodstream upon helping others.
cards.lore: True altruism exists; the biological machinery makes giving measurably more blissful than taking.
cards.gradeReason: Play it and you're the one who gives everything away and loves it. Crystal clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: euphoric ink. Subject: squirrel showering acorns onto others, brain lighting up electric blue. Mood: infectious joy.

cards.power: Causes generous actions to cascade through a social network like an airborne pathogen.
cards.lore: Goodness is infectious. One act of kindness infects the entire grid.
cards.gradeReason: One kind act, the ripples spread. You embody the contagion. No rules required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flowing ink. Subject: heart dropped in water, ripple rings expanding outward through frogs watching. Mood: spreading warmth.

cards.power: Overrides the instinct for self-preservation to protect vulnerable out-group members during a crisis.
cards.lore: The greatest heroes in history were raised with empathy and self-determination, not blind obedience.
cards.gradeReason: Classic hero archetype, morally grounded. Play it and you jump in without thinking.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rescue sketch. Subject: St Bernard dog leaping into icy water toward a stranger. Mood: instinctive courage.

cards.power: Nullifies authoritarian commands. Immune to the 'Just Following Orders' debuff.
cards.lore: A strict, positive upbringing breeds compliance; a free, empathic one breeds moral courage.
cards.gradeReason: Clear rebel role with moral weight. You know exactly what you refuse. Perfect G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: defiant ink. Subject: single sheep striding away from flock, chin raised. Mood: calm moral courage.

cards.power: Generates infinite energy and focus without the need for external rewards.
cards.lore: Humans are not naturally lazy; we are born as relentless, intrinsically motivated curiosity machines.
cards.gradeReason: Born curious. Play it and you become unstoppable. The anti-laziness manifesto card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wild ink. Subject: leopard cub surrounded by gears and sparks, pure manic curiosity. Mood: boundless exploration.

cards.power: Introduces cash rewards to a passion project, immediately killing the internal joy of doing it.
cards.lore: Financial incentives often destroy the very motivation they are designed to create.
cards.gradeReason: The villain who ruins everything with a paycheck. Devastating and immediately recognizable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corrupting ink. Subject: vulture dropping gold coins onto a canvas, paint turning grey. Mood: joyless transaction.

cards.power: Decreases participation rates when civic duty is replaced by market transactions.
cards.lore: Offering money for a moral act cheapens the social currency of the sacrifice.
cards.gradeReason: Interesting economics lesson but more seminar than stage—no clear role to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grim sketch. Subject: bat hanging over blood donation bag labelled with price tag. Mood: soiled altruism.

cards.power: Drains maximum psychological health by forcing the entity to perform meaningless, invisible tasks.
cards.lore: A lack of self-efficacy and purpose at work is a fast track to physical and mental illness.
cards.gradeReason: Three words, infinite recognition. The most relatable card in the deck. Instant embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: deadpan ink. Subject: rat in hamster wheel wearing a tie, staring into void. Mood: existential pointlessness.

cards.power: As resource hoarding increases, the entity's empathy and situational awareness stats plummet.
cards.lore: Massive wealth doesn't just buy luxury; it biologically dampens our compassion for the collective.
cards.gradeReason: Good visual metaphor but the stat-drop framing is more analytical than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical sketch. Subject: swan on money pile wearing golden blindfold. Mood: gilded obliviousness.

cards.power: Simulates a heavy alcohol-induced cognitive impairment while attempting to do three things at once.
cards.lore: The brain cannot parallel process focus; multitasking lowers your effective IQ to that of a drunk.
cards.gradeReason: Play this and immediately start doing three things badly. Comedy gold, instantly embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic ink. Subject: octopus juggling laptop, phone, coffee, sandwich with eyes crossed. Mood: confident incompetence.

cards.power: Merely placing this object on a table instantly degrades the depth and empathy of any conversation.
cards.lore: Digital connectivity tools physically destroy the fragile architecture of real-world empathic presence.
cards.gradeReason: Relatable but slightly descriptive—needs someone to play the phone-addict role to activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: modern ink. Subject: two swans face-to-face with a smartphone wall between them. Mood: disconnected proximity.

cards.power: Clears all 'Stress' and 'Depression' debuffs simply by standing near it for 20 minutes.
cards.lore: The natural world is a potent, side-effect-free medication for the modern nervous system.
cards.gradeReason: Healing utility card, well-framed but more descriptive than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: peaceful ink. Subject: badger leaning against ancient oak, stress visibly dissolving. Mood: restorative stillness.

cards.power: Shapes external reality to perfectly match the user's darkest, most cynical internal assumptions.
cards.lore: Our view of human nature is not just an observation; it is a blueprint we hand others to live out.
cards.gradeReason: Classic concept but names a phenomenon rather than creating a character to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychological ink. Subject: hedgehog surrounded by spines that form the shape of his own fears. Mood: self-created trap.

cards.power: Converts the pursuit of status symbols into chronic, systemic biological inflammation.
cards.lore: A life dedicated solely to acquiring things is interpreted by the body as a state of constant threat.
cards.gradeReason: Important science, but biological inflammation as a card mechanic is too clinical to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tense sketch. Subject: crow hunched over bag of gold surrounded by storm clouds. Mood: acquisitive anxiety.

cards.power: Decreases inflammatory genes and boosts immunity through the pursuit of deep, meaningful purpose.
cards.lore: Hedonic pleasure is fleeting, but a life of meaning changes your very genetic expression.
cards.gradeReason: Great concept, the Greek terminology needs unpacking but meaning vs. pleasure split is clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: glowing ink. Subject: bees building honeycomb shaped like DNA helix. Mood: purposeful creation.

cards.power: Forces the observer to mathematically overestimate the selfishness of everyone around them.
cards.lore: We are systematically blind to the goodness around us; people are vastly more cooperative than we think.
cards.gradeReason: Strong anti-cynic framing, but phantom needs a moment to click before it drives behavior.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: illusion ink. Subject: sheep-monster shadow on wall cast by ordinary rabbit. Mood: imagined threat.

cards.power: Bestows a massive behavioral upgrade simply by telling an entity they are naturally helpful.
cards.lore: People rise to the exact level of the expectations you place upon them.
cards.gradeReason: Play it, tell someone they're naturally good—watch the table transform. Immediate action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: transformation sketch. Subject: dog reading GOOD BOY label in mirror, chest swelling. Mood: identity activated.

cards.power: Permanently slows the cognitive development and trust-metrics of targeted offspring.
cards.lore: Authoritarian violence against children doesn't create discipline; it creates neurological damage.
cards.gradeReason: Dark and real, lands hard—but weight makes it more discussion card than performative trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: stark ink. Subject: comet striking fragile neural web. Mood: irreversible impact.

cards.power: Drains the target's life force by withholding acknowledgment for their hard work.
cards.lore: A lack of appreciation is deadlier to human motivation than a lack of resources.
cards.gradeReason: Resonant concept, needs a withholding manager character to fully activate at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: depleted sketch. Subject: peacock tail drooping, audience turned away. Mood: invisible effort.

cards.power: Mimics the dopamine hit of friendship while providing zero of the biological immunity benefits.
cards.lore: Social media is junk food for the social brain—it fills the stomach but starves the cells.
cards.gradeReason: Junk food for the social brain. Every player knows this feeling. Immediate recognition.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: web sketch. Subject: spider web glowing like phone screen, insect flies toward it. Mood: beautiful trap.

cards.power: Installs an uncontrollable hardware reflex that forces you to feel another's pain as your own.
cards.lore: Empathy isn't a choice or a moral high ground; it is an involuntary mirroring of the nervous system.
cards.gradeReason: Neuroscience lecture framing. Mirror neurons is a concept to explain, not a role to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: neural ink. Subject: chimpanzee grimacing in sync with another's pain across a gap. Mood: involuntary resonance.

cards.power: Tricks a hyper-social species into believing there isn't enough to go around, triggering panic protocols.
cards.lore: Greed is usually a trauma response to the manufactured illusion of scarcity.
cards.gradeReason: Smart critique, needs the who manufactures it question answered to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: manipulation sketch. Subject: pelican hoarding fish while others starve around an empty-looking but full sea. Mood: manufactured panic.

cards.power: Establishes the ultimate winning game-theory strategy: Cooperate first, then mirror your partner.
cards.lore: The most mathematically successful strategy in nature is simple, forgiving, and fiercely reciprocal.
cards.gradeReason: Name is a dance move. Play it and you start a tango. Brilliant embodied game theory.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dance sketch. Subject: two flamingos in tango, mirroring each other perfectly. Mood: reciprocal elegance.

cards.power: Activates Mutually Assured Destruction to punish those who violate the sacred rule of fairness.
cards.lore: We will gladly sabotage our own economic gain if it means punishing a cheater.
cards.gradeReason: The fairness vigilante. You know this role. You've been this role. Immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hard-boiled sketch. Subject: badger flipping table with righteous fury, coins flying. Mood: principled destruction.

cards.power: Transmutes the chaotic, painful noise of survival into a coherent, beautiful narrative.
cards.lore: Without a 'why,' humans wither; with a 'why,' we can survive almost any 'how.'
cards.gradeReason: The storyteller archetype. Play it and you start making meaning out of chaos. Pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: narrative ink. Subject: raven weaving chaos-threads into a coherent tapestry. Mood: transformative authorship.

cards.power: Equates dark pessimism with intellectual superiority, blinding the user to actual data.
cards.lore: Cynicism masquerades as wisdom, but it is scientifically the most inaccurate view of humanity.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect villain card. You've met this person. You may have been this person. Instant play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: smug ink. Subject: hyena in glasses smirking while data charts of human goodness glow behind. Mood: willful blindness.

cards.power: Proves that the long arc of the universe bends toward complexity, connection, and mutual aid.
cards.lore: The ultimate lesson of biology is that life prefers to build together rather than die alone.
cards.gradeReason: Grand philosophical sweep but no clear role—more closing argument than invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: epic sketch. Subject: crab on primordial shore, DNA strand stretching into cooperative future. Mood: cosmic cooperation.

cards.power: Erases the narrative that you are a selfish machine, granting you the freedom to choose cooperation.
cards.lore: You are an ultra-cooperative primate. The game is rigged, but you hold the pencil.
cards.gradeReason: Best name in the deck. Liberation theology in card form. Play it and you pick up a pencil.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: revolutionary sketch. Subject: rabbit erasing selfish-machine label with giant pencil, grinning. Mood: joyful defiance.

cards.power: Generates absolute loyalty and physical protection for those recognized as part of the 'In-Group.' We are capable of immense sacrifice, and the trick to world peace is expanding the definition of 'us.'
cards.gradeReason: Strong protector role, but in-group/out-group tension needs facilitation to perform well.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ancient sketch. Subject: mammoth herd forming protective circle, calves at center. Mood: fierce belonging.

cards.power: Regulates social behavior by broadcasting reputations across the collective grid at light-speed.
cards.lore: Language didn't evolve just to hunt mammoths; it evolved to warn the tribe about free-riders.
cards.gradeReason: Everyone knows the gossip network. Play it and you start broadcasting. Zero barrier.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: networked ink. Subject: birds on wire passing news beak to beak in a chain. Mood: rapid social intelligence.

cards.power: Resets your baseline happiness to zero immediately after acquiring a new material possession.
cards.lore: The brain quickly normalizes luxury; you cannot buy your way out of the human condition.
cards.gradeReason: Universally recognized trap. Play it and you're running. Nobody needs to explain it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Sisyphean sketch. Subject: greyhound sprinting on treadmill toward receding finish line. Mood: exhausted futility.

cards.power: Increases prosocial behavior by 50% simply by making the entity feel like it is being watched.
cards.lore: Even a mere picture of eyes on a wall forces the primate brain to adhere to cooperative norms.
cards.gradeReason: The all-seeing eye card. Play it and the whole table feels watched. Instant atmosphere shift.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surveillance ink. Subject: massive owl eye on wall, mouse below suddenly paying for coffee. Mood: observed morality.

cards.power: Drains the user's emotional reserves when exposed to infinite, unactionable global tragedies.
cards.lore: We evolved to care deeply about a core village of 150 people, not the agonizing suffering of 8 billion.
cards.gradeReason: Every social media user has lived this. Immediately recognizable, immediately performable collapse.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: exhausted ink. Subject: turtle retreating into shell, news headlines swirling outside. Mood: compassion depleted.

cards.power: Burns infinitely as long as the entity feels autonomy, mastery, and purpose.
cards.lore: You cannot ignite this flame from the outside; you can only provide the oxygen for it to burn.
cards.gradeReason: Beautiful metaphor but autonomy/mastery/purpose triad needs unpacking to perform at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: luminous ink. Subject: candle with moth flame, self-sustaining in darkness. Mood: inner light.

cards.power: Creates the toxic illusion that someone else's success requires your failure.
cards.lore: Love, trust, and knowledge are anti-fragile; they multiply when shared. The goblin is a liar.
cards.gradeReason: Goblin is a perfect archetype. You play it and you are immediately the petty competitor. Brilliant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: envious ink. Subject: goblin clutching a pie, watching neighbour's pie grow bigger. Mood: manufactured rivalry.

cards.power: Risks vulnerability in exchange for the chance to forge an unbreakable alliance.
cards.lore: Trust is the ultimate risk; but a society without trust is biologically and economically bankrupt.
cards.gradeReason: The gamble framing is good but needs a specific stake to make the risk feel real at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tense ink. Subject: small animal extending paw across table to larger predator. Mood: terrifying trust.

cards.power: Disarms the defensive mechanisms of hostile entities by showing your own soft underbelly first.
cards.lore: Connection requires the terrifying courage to be seen without your psychological armor.
cards.gradeReason: Resonant and true, but the loop mechanic needs context before players know how to trigger it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tender ink. Subject: tortoise showing underbelly to another, spines lowering in response. Mood: courageous openness.

cards.power: Rejects the cultural default of despair, actively searching for the cooperative signal in the noise.
cards.lore: In a world that profits from panic and cynicism, fierce optimism is an act of punk rebellion.
cards.gradeReason: Punk optimism. The most political card in the deck. Play it and stand up. Immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: punk sketch. Subject: raccoon holding umbrella upright in downpour, chin up. Mood: defiant hope.

cards.power: The ultimate win-state. Heals trauma, extends life, and generates infinite meaning.
cards.lore: The expedition ends where it began. We survive only when we sit by the fire together.
cards.gradeReason: The final card. Play it and everyone gathers. The whole deck has been building to this moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: primal warmth. Subject: bison, owl, fox, rabbit circling campfire under stars. Mood: homecoming.

cards.power: Allows the user to dictate the future of human evolution through their daily, microscopic choices.
cards.lore: The story of human nature isn't finished. You are the architect now. Draw carefully.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-invitation card. The player becomes the designer. Ultimate performative gesture.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: open sketch. Subject: blank card with pencil resting on it, FrizzleBob winking. Mood: open invitation.

verdict: This is the behavioral science textbook that became a card game without losing either its rigor or its comedy—and that is a very hard trick to pull off. The naming is the strongest in the corpus: THE BULLSHIT JOB, THE FLUFFY ANARCHIST, THE ZERO-SUM GOBLIN, THE LONELINESS SMOKER are all instant classics that need zero explanation and carry the whole deck. Chapter structure gives it rare narrative coherence: 56 cards feel like a journey, not a pile. The G3 cluster in Chapters 6 and 8 (Blood Money Paradox, Materialistic Stressor, Empathy Mirror) reads more like seminar slides than wrestling invitations—these need a character to inhabit, not a statistic to report. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: The evolutionary, psychological, and neurological case that humans are fundamentally decent—repackaged as a card-game brawl. For anyone who has ever argued that people are basically good and needed better ammunition.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 14 card pages (2x2 grid) = 56 cards. Chapter structure (8 chapters + 2 expansion sets + final chapter) is rare and gives the deck a genuine narrative arc. No RAF dice boxes. Power/lore text in standard fonts—no decorative baked-in font artifacts. The TRIBAL SHIELD card (p.13) has an unusually long POWER block that may double as lore—no separate LORE field visible. PDF created 2026-05-29 from iOS Quartz, clean resolution.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: HUMAN NATURE UNCUT (Hilfe, ich bin ein Mensch) – The Long Walk From Lone Wolf to the Village Fire (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Fifty-six cards, eight chapters, one expedition: from the selfish-ape bedtime story to the campfire it was invented to keep you away from.

Cynicism does not arrive as an opinion. It arrives as a blueprint. Tell a primate long enough that everyone is out for themselves and it starts hedging, hoarding, bolting the door against neighbors who were never coming for it. That is the engine this deck takes apart: the self-fulfilling prophecy that pays off for whoever sold you the lock. The opponent here is not a villain in a chair. It is the ambient hum that calls decency naïve, swears you are one missed paycheck from eating the neighbors, and quietly insists the fire is for someone else.

This is Social Story Wrestling at full length. You draw a card, perform it out loud like you mean it, and the table rules on whether it survives being said in front of other people. Uncut is the whole route: fifty-six cards across eight chapters and the expansion sets, a march that starts at evolution's cooperation engine and refuses to stop until everyone is sitting around THE VILLAGE HEARTH.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Human Nature Uncut Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring THE BULLSHIT JOB (the meaningless gig that drains your health bar one invisible task at a time), THE FLUFFY ANARCHIST (the rabbit who erases the selfish-machine label and hands you back the pencil), and THE LONELINESS SMOKER (isolation doing fifteen-cigarettes-a-day of quiet damage to the meat-sack).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and a table that decides whether the card you just argued still stands.
- The Eight-Chapter Expedition: a built route, not a pile, walking from cooperation and social wiring through the justice instinct, the modern toxins that isolate us, and the mindset moves that flip a cynic back into a neighbor, ending at THE VILLAGE HEARTH and THE BLANK CARD, the one that hands the future of the species to your next small choice.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this once and you are inside the Hilfe, ich bin ein Mensch cycle. Every future chapter, expansion, and topic deck in this series lands in your library as a free update. No second checkout, no upsell, no committee to clear it. You buy the expedition, you keep getting the map.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I'm a physician and artist. I keep rebuilding this one because the lone-wolf story is the only diagnosis I have ever met that makes the patient sicker the longer they believe it. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Teach with it, play it, run it at a table that needs the reminder. Want to support the craft? Every euro goes straight into the time I spend drawing and revising the next cards.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Human nature was never settled science handed down to you. It is a blank card, a pencil, and a fire worth walking back to."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
